title: BYO corpus record — msteams
description: A Microsoft Teams channel message. There is no title; `subject` is optional. A record with `replies` becomes a root post; each reply is served at `…/messages/{id}/replies` and only the root shows in the channel's message list, which is what `GET /channels/{id}/messages` returns.

content.description: The retrieval payload, served verbatim as the message's `body.content` (a system event's body is `<systemEventMessage/>` instead).

channel.description: The channel this message belongs to. Its `displayName`; the served `19:…@thread.tacv2` id is derived from it.

group.description: ACL group owning the channel (default: slug(channel)); null means the channel owns no group, so nothing is group-scoped to it.

author_name.description: The sender's display name, used for their principal entry and served as `from.user.displayName`.

visibility.description: public = org-wide (a `standard` channel), group = the channel's group, private = the post's speakers (its author and everyone who replies), who are its members by having posted in it. Anything other than public makes the channel `private` in `membershipType`.

readers.description: Explicit reader principals. `user:<email>` / `group:<id>` / `org:<name>` state the type; unprefixed, an address is a user and anything else a group. Overrides visibility — and an EMPTY array means nobody may read the document (admin-only), not everybody.

subject.description: The message's `subject`, in plaintext. Teams shows one only where the poster typed it; a message without one is served with the empty string.

message_type.description: Graph's `messageType` (default: message). `systemEventMessage` is a notice Teams itself generated (a member joined): it carries no `from`, its body is `<systemEventMessage/>`, and it is served as `unknownFutureValue` unless the request sends `Prefer: include-unknown-enum-members`.

content_type.description: The `body.contentType` this content is written in (default: text).

items.description: One chatMessageReaction. `reactionType` and `user` are required because Graph's own metadata declares both non-nullable, along with `createdDateTime` — a reaction real Graph could not send is not one a corpus should be able to write. `user` is an ADDRESS, not Graph's identitySet: the router builds that from it, the same way it builds a message's `from` from `author_email`. Give an address the corpus names elsewhere, so the user id served here resolves at `/users/{id}`.

reactionType.description: The emoji, as Graph serves it (e.g. 👍, 😢, 🎉). `like`, the name Graph's older enum used for 👍, is read as 👍.

createdDateTime.description: When they reacted (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). Defaults to the message's own time, since Graph declares this non-nullable and a reaction has to carry one.

displayName.description: The reaction's name (e.g. Like). Default: the name Teams gives the emoji, for the ones Backlot knows.

reactions.description: Reactions to this message. `chatMessageReaction` is a closed type in Graph's metadata and declares `reactionType`, `createdDateTime` and `user` non-nullable, so the shape is enforced here rather than passed through.

attachments.description: Files shared in this message. Each becomes a `reference` chatMessageAttachment, the shape a file shared in a channel takes; the body names it with `<attachment id="…"></attachment>`.

id.description: The id the body's `<attachment>` tag names (default: a GUID derived from the message).

mentions.description: The people this message @-mentions, in the order the body's `<at id="0">…</at>` tags number them. Each becomes a chatMessageMention whose `mentioned.user` the router builds from the address.

mentionText.description: The text the body shows inside the `<at>` tag (default: the person's display name).

edited.description: When the message was last edited (epoch seconds or ISO 8601), served as `lastEditedDateTime`. Absent means it never was, which the API reports as null.

created.description: Creation time (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). Sets `createdDateTime`, and the second the message id is drawn from.

items.description: A reply to this post — a full message that inherits the root's channel and ACL, and carries the root's id as its `replyToId`. Its time is its own `created`.

doc_id.description: Optional stable id for the reply.

created.description: Reply time. Backlot requires a later second than the preceding message in an imported thread; this is an emulator constraint, not a Microsoft limit.
